findings.message: reactive accessor "count" is read in a callback written in rendering function and passed to a consumer that is not proven to invoke it during the call or component rendering; that consumer may invoke it then, later from a closure it returns or keeps, or never, so whether this read runs untracked in rendering function cannot be proven either way
findings.hint: Move the read into a tracking scope: JSX, a createMemo, or the compute function of createEffect(compute, apply). If a one-time snapshot is intended, wrap the read in untrack() to make that explicit. If this read executes untracked in dev, Solid warns STRICT_READ_UNTRACKED for it; this finding does not establish that it does, so confirm the read's actual execution and tracking status before relying on that warning.

findings.message: setter "setCount" is called in Migrated, but no compiler or semantic fact places where this code runs, so whether it runs under a children-capable owner, where Solid throws, cannot be proven either way
findings.hint: Derive the value instead of writing it back: replace compute-then-set with a createMemo. If the write is genuinely imperative, move it to an event handler, an action, the apply function of createEffect(compute, apply), or a leaf scope (onSettled, createTrackedEffect). Wrapping the write in untrack() does not help: the guard keys on the owner, not on tracking. For an internal reactive signal only, opt in with { ownedWrite: true } in that signal's creation options; a store setter has no such opt-in.
